subject: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@greencloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the upload to the publisher portal earlier today. I pulled a quick pass on the manifest and there are a few fields that will block Microsoft’s technical validation and the co-sell registration step unless we reconcile them:

- OfferId vs PublisherId mismatch: the manifest lists PublisherId as GC-PUB-2024 while the portal shows GC-PUB-2025. We need the portal Publisher ID to match the manifest exactly.
- SKU fulfillment type: one SKU is marked as "Virtual Machine" but this is a SaaS offer and must use SaaSFulfillment.
- Entitlement mapping: the skuProperties are missing the pci_level and user_quota keys we recommend for co-sell reporting.
- Identity and SSO: your manifest references an unsupported redirect URL schema for the managed identity.

I attached a small template (initial_manifest_template.json) with annotated comments — could you drop your draft into that and re-send? Also attaching the SKU mapping worksheet I normally use to align telemetry fields.

Proposed next steps:
1) You update manifest with PublisherId and SKU changes and return by EOD Mon (3/17).
2) We run a pre-validation check on Tue (3/18) and then schedule a 30-min publisher verification call with Microsoft to complete the technical gate.

If that timeline is tight, tell me which dates work and we’ll flex.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial_manifest_template.json (stub), azure-sku-mapping.xlsx (stub)
From: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@greencloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenCloud Marketplace Team <marketplace@greencloud.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick review and the template. Apologies for the PublisherId drift; we rotated publisher IDs during our fiscal housekeeping and I must have uploaded the wrong bundle. I attached our draft manifest and a couple of screenshots from the portal showing the PublisherId and the SKU listing.

Questions from our side:
- For SaaSFulfillment, do we need to implement the full Fulfillment API before validation, or is a stubbed endpoint acceptable for the tech gate?
- On entitlements: you mentioned pci_level — our product currently only distinguishes standard vs enterprise. Will you accept pci_level as a metadata string?

We can aim to get the updated manifest to you by EOD Mon. If Microsoft requires the Fulfillment API in place for the verification call we may need to move the call to late next week — want to confirm the requirement first.

Attachments: greencloud_manifest_v1.json (draft), pub-portal-screenshot.png

Best,
Anna Gomez
Head of Marketplace, GreenCloud Solutions
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@greencloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling

Hi Anna — looping in a few technical clarifications that should make the verification smoother.

1) SaaS Fulfillment API: Microsoft’s tech gate typically accepts a testable endpoint that returns the required JSON schema (subscriptionId, planId, fulfillmentState) — it does not need to be fully wired to billing at validation time. A stub endpoint that returns valid responses for test subscriptions is acceptable. Document: https://aka.ms/marketplace-saas-fulfillment (referenced).

2) Entitlement metadata: yes, PCI level may be passed as a freeform string in the sku.properties object, but add a corresponding telemetry_key so co-sell reporting can map it later. Example: "sku.properties.pci_level": "SA-1" and "sku.properties.telemetry_key": "gc_pci_level".

3) PublisherId: confirm you will use the portal value GC-PUB-2025. If you have any signed publisher transfer docs we can attach to the submission; otherwise ensure the manifest line is updated.

4) SSO / Redirect URIs: Please switch to an https-based redirect URI for the managed identity flow; non-https schemas cause an automatic rejection.

Marcus — once Anna pushes the corrected manifest we’ll run it through our manifest linter and then I’ll do a quick live validation (curl + sample payloads).

— Soojin
Technical Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@greencloud.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling

Thanks Soojin — that's clear and helpful. Anna: we’re good to proceed with your Monday update as proposed. A couple of coordination items for co-sell ops and legal: 

- Marissa from our Marketplace Ops team will handle the co-sell registration paperwork and ensure the incentive mapping is set for your account. Marissa — can you confirm what documentation you need from GreenCloud to open the co-sell request with Microsoft?
- Karthik — please prepare the pre-validation runbook (curl examples and sample payloads) once we get the updated manifest.

Action items for GreenCloud (Anna):
1) Update manifest: PublisherId -> GC-PUB-2025; change the SKU type to SaaSFulfillment; add sku.properties.pci_level and telemetry_key.
2) Push a stub SaaS Fulfillment endpoint that returns successful test payloads for planId: test-plan-001.
3) Share any publisher transfer documentation if the portal PublisherId was recently changed.

I’ll coordinate a 30-min verification slot on Wed 3/18 at 3:00pm PT with the Microsoft contact. If that conflicts, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Marcus
Attachments: azure-sku-mapping.xlsx (stub)
From: Anna Gomez <anna.gomez@greencloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Azure offer manifest review and co-sell scheduling

Marcus / team —

All right, we made the manifest edits and pushed a stub endpoint to https://api.greencloud.com/saas/test-fulfillment (returns sample payloads). I attached the updated manifest and a short SKU mapping sheet.

We can make the 3:00pm PT slot on Wed 3/18 for the verification call — Michael, will you be able to join or should we expect an MS engineering rep?

I attached a calendar invite (calendar-invite.ics) — please accept and I’ll send dial-in details.

Thanks for the quick turn.
Anna
Attachments: greencloud_manifest_v1.json (updated), azure-sku-mapping.xlsx (updated), calendar-invite.ics
